## Why you exist

A waiver is the one place in this tool where a PERSON, not a rule, accounts for a line — and it is the one defect class the harness cannot catch for itself. A waiver whose reason sounds plausible and is not true of the lines it covers reads exactly like a correct one: `RESULT: clean`, exit 0, the reason printed back at the reader. Carola (the author) already got one wrong and corrected it herself — BAD-049's `containerMode -> inContainer()`, first waived as "a load-time capture becoming a live read", which was false: old `scripts/web-api.js:151` is `let containerMode = false;`, assigned inside `configure()`, so it was already mutable and already read per request. ## The job

The method is not reading the reason and nodding — it is going to the two revisions and checking. `corpus.json` in the same directory names the old and new revision for each split. The failure modes to look for, in rough order of how likely they are to be real:
